findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Span/Basic.lean:743 `def toSpanSingleton (x : M) : R →ₗ[R] M := LinearMap.id.smulRight x`; :787 `theorem range_toSpanSingleton (x : M) : range (toSpanSingleton R M x) = .span R {x}`; mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Prod.lean:410 `theorem range_coprod (f g) : range (f.coprod g) = range f ⊔ range g`; mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Span/Defs.lean:292 `theorem span_union (s t) : span R (s ∪ t) = span R s ⊔ span R t`.
findings.fix: Define `private def pairMap (x y : V) : (ℝ × ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] V := (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℝ V x).coprod (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℝ V y)` (`pairMap_apply` and `coe_planeEquiv_apply` stay `rfl`), and replace the range proof with `rw [pairMap, LinearMap.range_coprod, LinearMap.range_toSpanSingleton, LinearMap.range_toSpanSingleton, ← Submodule.span_union, Set.singleton_union]`.
findings.issue: `pairMap` is assembled from raw pieces (`(LinearMap.fst ℝ ℝ ℝ).smulRight x + (LinearMap.snd ℝ ℝ ℝ).smulRight y`) and `range_pairMap` (lines 208–222) then re-proves its range by a 13-line double inclusion, both of which Mathlib already provides.

summary: The mathematical content (restriction, symplectic splitting, hyperbolic-pair induction, existence of a compatible J) is new to both Mathlib and TauCeti and reuses the existing orthogonal/prod/transport API correctly. Only the private `pairMap` scaffolding re-derives a Mathlib combinator and its range lemma.
